facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant took part in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it became apparent that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the meeting at Bolotnaya Square to finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
It took the police about two hours to clear Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
On 8 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 8 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having used violence against the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 9 June 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered that the applicant be placed in pre-trial detention until 8 August 2012.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, referred to the gravity of the charges against the applicant.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, stated that if at liberty the applicant could co-ordinate his position with accomplices who had yet to be discovered and whose identities were still being established by the investigation.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to flee to avoid the investigation and trial.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to continue his criminal activity if at liberty.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to destroy evidence or otherwise obstruct the investigation if at liberty.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, noted that the criminal case was still at an initial stage.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 18 May 2012 the criminal case file was transferred from the Moscow city department to the headquarters of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation for further investigation.
On 28 May 2012 an investigation was launched into the criminal offence of organising acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 the two criminal cases (mass disorder/violence against police, and organising mass disorder) were joined into a single criminal case.
The applicant was accused of attempting to break through the police cordon at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was accused of throwing pieces of tarmac and stones at Police Officer K. at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The applicant's alleged throwing of pieces of tarmac and stones at Police Officer K. was accused of having caused Police Officer K. a broken finger.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue and to defy the lawful orders of the police.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the unidentified persons' calls led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials in connection with the performance of their duties and the destruction of property.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that at 5 p.m. at the latest on 6 May 2012 the defendants acquired the criminal intent to participate in mass disorder and to use violence against police officers.
On 9 June 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered that the applicant be placed in pre-trial detention until 8 August 2012.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, referred to the gravity of the charges against the applicant.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, stated that if at liberty the applicant could co-ordinate his position with accomplices who had yet to be discovered and whose identities were still being established by the investigation.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to flee to avoid the investigation and trial.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to continue his criminal activity if at liberty.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to destroy evidence or otherwise obstruct the investigation if at liberty.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its detention order of 9 June 2012, noted that the criminal case was still at an initial stage.
On 6 August 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow granted the investigator's application and extended the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 November 2012.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 6 August 2012, considered that the circumstances justifying the detention order had not changed.
On 12 September 2012 the Moscow City Court upheld the extension order of 6 August 2012 issued by the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow.
On 30 October 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow granted an extension of the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 March 2013.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 30 October 2012, noted that the circumstances justifying the detention order had not changed, essentially on the same grounds as earlier.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its extension orders of 1 March 2013 and 22 April 2013, considered that the circumstances justifying the detention order had not changed.
On 10 April 2013 the Moscow City Court upheld the extension order of 1 March 2013 issued by the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow.
On 30 May 2013 the Moscow City Court upheld the extension order of 22 April 2013 issued by the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 6 June 2013, based its decision on the gravity of the charges and its finding that the reasons which initially warranted the detention had not changed.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 6 June 2013, found that no other measures of restraint would secure the aims and goals of the judicial proceedings.

The applicant's request for an alternative preventive measure was dismissed by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow on 6 June 2013 on the grounds that no other measure could secure the proper course of justice in the case.
On 19 November 2013 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow granted an extension of detention in respect of nine defendants, including the applicant.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 19 November 2013, ordered the detention of the nine defendants, including the applicant, until 24 February 2014.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 19 November 2013, based its decision on the gravity of the charges and the nature of the offences imputable to the defendants.
On 17 December 2013 the Moscow City Court upheld the extension order of 19 November 2013 issued by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.
The applicant's pre-trial detention counted towards his prison sentence.
The applicant was held in remand prison IZ-77/5 for the whole period of his pre-trial detention from 20 June 2012.
The applicant was held in four different cells in remand prison IZ-77/5 during his pre-trial detention.
The applicant did not provide any description of the conditions of his detention in remand prison IZ-77/5.
The applicant submitted that the convoy room of the Moscow City Court was poorly lit.
The applicant submitted that access to the toilet in the convoy room of the Moscow City Court was limited to once an hour.
The applicant submitted that he had been required to strip naked and to perform sit-ups during the body search conducted in the convoy room of the Moscow City Court.
The defendants, including the applicant, were held in glass cabins in hearing room no. 338 and hearing room no. 635 at the Moscow City Court.
From mid-September 2013 to the end of 2013 the hearings continued at the Nikulinskiy District Court of Moscow in hearing room no. 303.
In January and February 2014 the hearings took place at the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow in hearing room no. 410.

Hearing room no. 303 at the Nikulinskiy District Court of Moscow and hearing room no. 410 at the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow were equipped with metal cages in which nine defendants (eight from 19 December 2013), including the applicant, sat during the hearings.
For a detailed description of the conditions in the hearing rooms used during the trial, see Yaroslav Belousov v. Russia (nos. 2653/13 and 60980/14, §§ 74-77, 4 October 2016).
